title: Quantitative photoconversion analysis of internal molecular dynamics in stress granules and other membraneless organelles in live cells
protocol: Form membraneless compartments using sodium arsenite for 1 hour.
Use sodium arsenite at a concentration of 200 μM for stress granule formation.
Replace the media in the glass-bottom plate with stress granule induction solution (200 μM arsenite in the media).
Incubate the plate for 1 hour in a cell culture incubator at 37°C/5% CO2.
Introduce the plate into a live-cell imaging chamber preheated to 37°C.
Photoconvert a portion of the membraneless compartment.
Photoswitch Dendra2 irreversibly to track protein diffusion and degradation.
Use Dendra2 photoswitching to monitor protein degradation.
Photoconvert a small portion (< half) of the membraneless compartment.
Prepare the setup for the photoconversion of stress granule compartments.
Zoom in on the cell until the stress granule compartment is clearly visible and centered.
Position the photoactivation point on the stress granule.
Manually adjust the photoactivation point if the cell moves at the beginning of imaging.
Align the digital point with the actual photoconversion position.
Contact the technician to realign the system or manually adjust it using the software if necessary.
Set the photoconversion parameters including laser power, pulse duration, and number of pulses.
Initiate the photoconversion manually with a pulse duration of 100 ms.
Photoconvert the portion of the stress granule by starting the acquisition.
Visualize both pre-photoconversion (488 nm excitation) and post-photoconversion (561 nm excitation) channels during the acquisition.
Use the same photoconversion parameters and timing of acquisition between repeats and conditions.
Set a protocol in the system: photoconvert in 1 s after start of the movie, pulse of 200 ms, duration of acquisition 5 s.
Track the diffusion immediately following photoconversion with less than 5-10 s interval.
Set up a 2D time-lapse acquiring an image every 1 minute for 15 minutes.
Use the same position and magnification as used for the photoconversion.
Photoconvert the fluorescent protein using a rate of 30 frames per second.
Take a movie with only 16 frames in 15 minutes to reduce bleaching.
Establish critical parameters for photoconversion and tracking duration after the first run.
Repeat steps from formation/treatment of membraneless compartments to photoconversion and tracking N times for each treatment.
Quantify the fluorescence intensity of the photoconverted area.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of an immediately adjacent area along the long axis of the stress granule.
Record the fluorescence intensity over 15 minutes from the start of the movie.
Determine the diffusion time when the fluorescence intensity in the photoconverted and adjacent areas equalizes within a 5% margin.
